correctness.rationale: With q=2^n, each world is an iid uniform vector in [q]^r, and a size-a projection has expected collision count binom(m,2)/q^a->lambda=c^2/2. Expanding mixed factorial moments across all critical A, disjoint world-pairs contribute lambda^K; connected shared-vertex components v>=3 cost O(q^{a(1-v/2)}) and multiply marked two-vertex edges with different A force >=a+1 coordinate agreements and cost O(q^-1). Hence the critical vector converges to independent Poisson(lambda) coordinates. For |A|>a, Markov kills all collisions; for |A|<a and j outside A, violating pair indicators are pairwise independent even when pairs share one world, and their count has mean tending to infinity, so all nontrivial implications fail simultaneously. Critical collision-free indicators become independent Bernoulli(e^-lambda), yielding the binomial number of minimal size-a determinants. Reconstructed all A,B, including empty antecedents, fixed r,a,c; independent exhaustive finite q=3, r=3, m=3 enumeration verifies means/cross covariance but not the limit.
